meta.description: Tests gene lists and ranked vectors against live or dated WikiPathways collections with clusterProfiler and rWikiPathways.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All numerical evidence is fresh synthetic/live WikiPathways output with its release date and data source stated; no biomedical claim was invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill performs pathway enrichment on de-identified gene lists and makes no individual diagnostic or treatment claim.

methodological_ground.detail: ORA, ranked GSEA, explicit universes, Entrez matching, live-data drift, and dated GMT pinning were each exercised and correctly distinguished.

code_usability.detail: The shipped rWikiPathways-only direct-query/other-organisms guidance calls get_wp_organisms(), which is not exported by rWikiPathways 1.30.0 and errors when followed as written. clusterProfiler happens to export a same-named function, masking the defect in one separate example.

functional_suitability.note: ORA, GSEA, dated pinning, direct API inspection, and organism coverage are well scoped, but a documented rWikiPathways command is invalid in its stated import context.

reliability.note: Strong warnings about IDs, universe, archive retention, and community curation; the wrong namespace function defeats the stated organism-validation guard.

performance_context.note: The Skill has a bounded workflow, records live-data behavior, and uses a retry window for monthly releases.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree, workflow, and recovery guidance are unusually explicit, but an agent following the direct-query block is stopped before the advertised organism check.

human_usability.note: Readable scenario guidance and a concise usage guide mitigate necessarily technical pathway content.

security.note: No credentials, destructive actions, or untrusted-code execution are documented; public archive/API traffic is identified.

maintainability.note: The pinned procedure is factored into a shipped script and source files are organized, but the version-compatible API boundary was not kept current.

agent_specific.note: Excellent trigger, scope, and escape-hatch language; the `get_wp_organisms()` mismatch makes a key self-check unreliable.

key_strengths: Fresh private-runtime execution confirms live ORA, ranked GSEA, explicit-universe behavior, dated archive pinning, and both shipped examples.
The dated-GMT script successfully picks an available monthly release and writes a reproducible result with the used release date.
The Skill accurately teaches the large background-universe inflation effect and the community-curation limitations of WikiPathways.

recommendations.title: Replace the invalid rWikiPathways organism accessor
recommendations.problem: The direct-query and other-organisms guidance says that get_wp_organisms() belongs to rWikiPathways, but rWikiPathways 1.30.0 does not export it. An agent following the stated library(rWikiPathways)-only code errors before it can validate the organism string.
recommendations.root_cause: The documentation conflates clusterProfiler::get_wp_organisms with rWikiPathways' API and the Version Compatibility section does not protect the namespace boundary.
recommendations.fix: Use rWikiPathways::listOrganisms() everywhere the code loads rWikiPathways alone, or explicitly import and namespace clusterProfiler::get_wp_organisms(). Re-run the standalone direct-query block and a non-human organism check in the declared compatible runtime.
